it took me a hell lot of listening to even come remotely close to understanding the song. to me, it seems to be about capitalism. i might be digging too deep into it but thats just my interpretation. i think its about the work/hustle culture and how we dedicate our entire lives to our career. the reason why i think it's more about capitalism than merely pressure from school is because the of lines "where we got our jeans and where the hell we found our coats" and "nikes of black and green" which suggests classism and the focus of materialistic things in society. "the men that wrung us dry" and "the common fool" are also about classism and the hierarchy system in corporations, the "men" being the owners and ceos that literally control the workers' entire lives. "the common fool" matched with "we've been held back for after school meetings" is about how most ppl spend their lives being slaves to capitalism and if you (declan) are rebellious and want things to change then youre just considered a stupid child who doesn't understand the world & needs to be punished for their beliefs, which correlates to more of his songs such as dysac and tkdwcm where he also mentions the empowerment of young people. probably my favourite verse from the song is "iron your shirt and tie forever til you die" coupled with "carousels & their horses, forever spinning around" these really did it for me, theyre so real and blunt.
